card.name: Wry words in humorous web prose
card.fires_on: Words in the middle of a phrase in jokey, mock-formal web writing, such as 'the safety of my truck' or 'pure, unadulterated luck'. The marked word is often an elevated or ironic adjective, noun or linking word.

modes.label: Mock-grand wording
modes.description: An elevated or ironic word in a humorous narrative, often right before the noun it describes.
modes.example: Upon retreating to the<< safety>> of my truck I discovered the aroma retreated

modes.label: Linking words in a joke phrase
modes.description: A small linking word or comma inside a witty or quoted phrase.
modes.example: democracy might be considered the worst form of government except<< for>> all the others.

card.writes: It suppresses cheerful slang such as yay, yummy and awesome, and mildly favors formal or literal continuations.
card.plain: It fires on dry, tongue-in-cheek humor in casual web writing, where the next word is not an enthusiastic one.
